sources.title: Rock climbing in Leonidio
sources.notes: Guidebook publisher page; used for limestone, sport and multipitch character.

sections.heading: Hero
sections.body: A major mainland Greek limestone base with more than 3,000 routes, red and grey walls, sport crags and bolted multi-pitches above a working town.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body:
Leonidio is one of the big modern Greek limestone destinations. The climbing sits around the town, with red and grey walls rising above the valley and enough sectors to make the area feel like a full winter and shoulder-season base rather than a single famous crag.

The appeal is breadth. You can build a trip around friendly sport mileage, harder tufa lines, steep walls or fully bolted longer routes, then return each day to a real town with visitor accommodation and food close at hand.

sections.heading: History and context
sections.body: Leonidio's reputation has grown around high-volume sport climbing and a strong local climbing scene. It now sits alongside the better-known Greek islands as a serious limestone destination, with the advantage of mainland access and a town directly below the crags.
warnings: No sourced history and context content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Rock and climbing character
sections.body:
Expect red and grey limestone, generally well bolted, with single-pitch sport routes and fully bolted multi-pitch lines. The style ranges from slabs and vertical walls to steep tufa climbing, so route choice matters more than chasing one headline sector.

The limestone can feel very different from wall to wall: technical feet on lower-angle terrain, pumpy sequences on steeper ground and long pitches where resting well is part of the grade.

sections.heading: Who it suits
sections.body:
Leonidio works for a wide span of sport climbers. The supported grade spread starts low enough for mileage days and runs into very hard climbing, so mixed groups can usually build sensible plans if they choose sectors carefully.

It is especially useful for climbers who want a proper destination rhythm: several climbing days, rest-day options, town logistics and enough route variety to adjust around weather and skin.

sections.heading: Grades and difficulty
sections.body: The supported scale is over 3,000 routes, with grades from F3 to F9a+. That makes Leonidio one of the broadest entries in this batch and gives the page enough confidence to speak about both accessible and elite-level sport climbing.

sections.heading: Season and conditions
sections.body: Spring, autumn and winter are the best planning windows for this file. Summer is left as an avoid season because heat is the obvious limiting factor for Mediterranean limestone, especially on sunny walls.

sections.heading: Gear and equipment
sections.body: Bring a sport rack sized for long single pitches, a rope appropriate for the chosen sector and a helmet for busy limestone areas. For multi-pitch days, add the normal personal kit for bolted longer routes rather than assuming every climb is a roadside sport pitch.
warnings: No sourced gear and equipment content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Transport and access
sections.body: Athens is the normal airport city for this mainland-Greece entry. A car is strongly recommended because the crags are spread around Leonidio and sector choice is central to managing grades, sun and conditions.

sections.heading: Where to stay
sections.body: Leonidio has the advantage of town-based logistics: hotels, guesthouses and apartments can all work for a climbing week. Keep specific lodging names out of the page until they are checked separately, but the broad accommodation picture is strong enough for trip planning.

sections.heading: Rest days
sections.body: Rest days can stay local. The town-and-coast setting gives easy low-effort days between climbing sessions, and the wider Peloponnese makes it possible to turn a climbing trip into a broader Greek travel week.
warnings: No sourced rest days content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Practical tips
sections.body: Use sector choice as the main tactic. With this many routes and aspects, a good day often comes from matching grade, sun and wind rather than forcing the most famous wall.
warnings: No sourced practical tips content found for this pass.

sections.heading: Safety notes
sections.body: Treat Leonidio as a large limestone area: wear a helmet where rockfall or busy routes make it sensible, check lower-offs and knots carefully on long pitches, and use current local information for any sector access changes.
warnings: No sourced safety notes content found for this pass.

sections.heading: FAQ
sections.body:
How big is Leonidio? This batch uses a supported figure of more than 3,000 routes.

Is it only hard climbing? No. The supported grade range runs from F3 to F9a+.

Do you need a car? Yes for practical sector access and weather tactics.
